principles: Every runtime-changing DONE completion site must pass through the same semver finalization contract.
Version state must be structurally synchronized, including lockfiles, before build or user-visible version checks are trusted.
Recovery must be idempotent and loud on failure; no silent skip when runtimeSemverChanged is true.
Do not broaden local version finalization into remote publish or product capability semver.
Keep the patch focused enough that existing DONE/recovery behavior and ledgers remain stable.
drivers: B-90d6 proved runtime changes can reach main without a new consumable version if finalization is bypassed.
Existing normal DONE path already has a bump hook; done_recover is the immediate missing completion site.
The current lockfile drift shows the three-point sync model is narrower than the documented version discipline.

options.name: A: Minimal finalizer parity plus lockfile sync
pros: Adds bumpVersionOnDoneMerge to done_recover before build with the existing changed-path predicate.
Extends the existing version-bump module instead of inventing a release manager.
Keeps remote release/publish unchanged and human-approved.
cons: Manual git fast-forward outside Lattice still cannot be fully prevented by this patch alone.
The first DONE of this story may need local CLI/dist awareness so the new lockfile-sync bump code is what runs.

options.name: B: New global release manager and DONE gate
pros: Could enforce every possible manual recovery path and centralize release policy.
Could add richer user prompts for defer/bump decisions.
cons: Much larger scope than the observed bug.
Higher risk of changing package semver and capability release semantics together.
Would delay the immediate B-90d6 version repair.

options.name: C: Only manually bump B-90d6 to 0.3.171
pros: Fastest visible repair for the current version number.
cons: Leaves done_recover able to miss future bumps.
Would not satisfy the mechanism issue the user asked to inspect and fix.

chosen: A: Minimal finalizer parity plus lockfile sync
rationale: Choose the smallest mechanism repair that directly closes the observed bug class: done_recover gets the same bump finalizer as normal DONE, the bump finalizer synchronizes lockfiles, and tests pin both behaviors without changing remote release policy.

preMortem.scenario: done_recover bump runs after build or not at all
preMortem.trigger: The patch adds bump code in the wrong order or only updates tests.
preMortem.consequence: Recovered runtime-changing stories can still finish with stale lattice --version.
preMortem.mitigation: Place bumpVersionOnDoneMerge immediately after changedPaths/runtimeSemverChanged calculation and before runDoneMainPackageBuildAfterMerge; assert output order in smoke.

preMortem.scenario: Lockfiles remain stale after auto bump
preMortem.trigger: VERSION_SYNC_PATHS excludes package-lock files or smoke fixture does not model them.
preMortem.consequence: Package metadata looks bumped but install/release tooling still sees old versions.
preMortem.mitigation: Add lockfiles to VERSION_SYNC_FILES/VERSION_SYNC_PATHS, read/verify their versions, and extend version-bump-smoke fixtures and assertions.

preMortem.scenario: Story DONE uses old global dist and misses the new lockfile-sync behavior
preMortem.trigger: Self-hosted global lattice binary points at main dist before this story merges.
preMortem.consequence: Final state after DONE has package/brand at 0.3.171 but lockfiles stale.
preMortem.mitigation: Build the story worktree and, if needed for DONE, run the worktree dist CLI so the new finalizer performs the merge/bump; verify final version sync afterward.

preMortem.trigger: Release scripts or git push are folded into the fix.
preMortem.consequence: Local story work leaks to origin without human release approval.
preMortem.mitigation: Do not run git push, npm publish, or scripts/release.mjs publish; verification explicitly checks local-only behavior.
